title: Colour the open chords
summary: Small, unfamiliar shapes are the bottleneck, not knowledge. This level trains the hand on exactly the shapes Reckoner needs — the high three-string triads of the riff and the thumb voicings of the bridge — alongside the one-finger colours (sus2, sus4, maj7, add9) of the open chords you already own, and the first numbers-in-a-key work in C and G. Here Comes the Sun brings the thumb-over D/F♯, sus hammer-ons and your first odd-meter bars.
goals: Reckoner start to finish with the record, in your teacher's voicings.
Here Comes the Sun with the record (capo 7), including the 11/8 bridge, counted.
30+ clean changes a minute between the Reckoner riff triads, and 25+ into and out of the bridge's thumb chord.
Turn any open A, D, C or G into its sus/maj7/add9 relative by moving one finger, without looking.
Play C and G major in open position in eighths, and name the six chords of each key by number.

reading.note: first, before Session A. If you read only one chapter, this is it.
week 1 — how to read the diagrams in this packet.
week 2 — skim; keep the table for reference.
week 2 — Session B uses it from week 3.

song_plan: Core: **Reckoner** (you are mid-way — where your teacher's voicing differs from the chart, use the teacher's and pencil it onto the chord page) and **Here Comes the Sun**. A week's section already solid? Take the next week's. Swap a core song for an alternate only when you can already play it with the record, or when its hard change is still under 15 a minute after two weeks; keep that hard change in Session A either way. Alternates, easiest first: *Good Feeling* (sus decorations), *The Book of Love* (thumb D/F♯), *The First Cut Is the Deepest* (rock-G anchors).

week_plan.fretboard: C major, open position. Chords of C: C Dm Em F G Am
week_plan.song: Reckoner intro riff. Here Comes the Sun verse

week_plan.chords: **1** D (11-10-10) ↔ Dsus4 (12-10-10) as a hammer-on · **2** open A → C/E (9-8-8), the verse ending · **3** Em7/G ↔ D/F♯ (thumb)
week_plan.fretboard: C major in 3rds. Sevenths of C: Cmaj7 Dm7 Em7 Fmaj7 G7 Am7
week_plan.song: Reckoner verse, into the riff. HCTS refrain

week_plan.chords: **1** Emaj7/G♯ (thumb) ↔ Em/G — no common fingers · **2** Cmaj7 ↔ B7/D♯ · **3** Em/G → Am → Cmaj7 (middle finger stays on string 4, fret 2)
week_plan.fretboard: G major, open position (= E minor). Chords of G: G Am Bm C D Em

week_plan.chords: **1** your weakest benchmark pair (log page) · **2–3** random pairs from the chord page
week_plan.fretboard: G major in 3rds. E minor from E to E; Em D C A = i ♭VII ♭VI IV
week_plan.song: Reckoner whole form, then with the record. HCTS with the record

chord_groups.label: Reckoner riff — top three strings (version A)
Here Comes the Sun and one-finger colours

exit_criteria: Benchmark pairs 1–4 at target (30 / 30 / 25 / 30 a minute) in two Session Ds in a row.
Reckoner start to finish with the record, your teacher's voicings, no stops.
Here Comes the Sun with the record, capo 7, bridge counted, no stops.
G major open position up and down in eighths at 80, from memory; then G Am Bm C D Em saying the numbers, no hesitation.
One-finger variations (A, D, C and rock-G lines) one bar each at 80 with eyes closed, every string clean.
stuck: Not every box ticked after 6 weeks? Move on anyway. Keep one song from this level (Reckoner, or an easier alternate) as a 5-minute play-through in Level 2's Session D, and open every Level 2 Session A primer with your weakest pair until it reaches 30.
skip_ahead: Pass every benchmark cold (first attempt, no practice that day) in week 1's Session D? Go straight to Level 2 and take Reckoner with you.

drills.title: One-minute changes
drills.instructions: Timer at 1:00. One down-strum per chord, change, strum the other, as fast as you can while staying clean. Count clean landings only: every string of the shape rings, no stray strings. Two rounds per pair; write the better count.

drills.title: Air shapes
drills.instructions: Hand off the neck. Form the whole shape an inch above the strings, land all fingers at once, strum once, check every string, lift. Ten per shape. On the triads, the index mini-barre and the middle finger land together.

drills.title: Place and lift
drills.instructions: Fret the shape, relax until the fingers just touch the strings, press again. Twenty presses, one per click at 60, no strumming. Use it on the thumb shapes (Emaj7/G♯ 466450, D/F♯ 2x0232) and the fret-12 Em/G.

drills.title: Anchor hunt
drills.instructions: Before a new pair, say aloud what stays (anchor), what slides along its string (guide) and what jumps. Then ten changes keeping anchors down and guides touching. This level: rock G → Cadd9 → Dsus4 → Em7 = fingers 3+4 stay on fret 3 of strings 2–1; Em/G → Am → Cmaj7 = middle stays on string 4 fret 2; the riff triads = index slides along strings 2–1.

drills.title: Slow motion
drills.instructions: Make the change over a slow count of five, every finger moving at once on the shortest path. Watch the fingers. Five slow, then five at normal speed.

drills.title: Change loop
drills.instructions: Strum chord 1 once, change, strum chord 2 once, stop, reset. Ten clean in a row; a miss sets the count back to zero.

drills.title: Tempo ladder
drills.instructions: One chord per bar, four down-strums. Start where the change is perfect (try 50). Three clean passes: +4 bpm. A miss: −8 bpm. Write the top clean tempo in today's blank.

drills.title: Bass first
drills.instructions: For thumb chords: on beat 1 play only the thumb note (G♯ for Emaj7/G♯, F♯ for D/F♯), then strum the rest on beat 2. Ten times; then land the thumb first in a single full strum.

drills.title: Eyes closed
drills.instructions: Make the change without looking. Open your eyes after landing to check. Ten times.

drills.title: Leave early
drills.instructions: Down-up eighths, four bars per chord. On the last “and” of each bar let go and strum the open strings while travelling. In Here Comes the Sun do it on every change.

drills.title: Song loop
drills.instructions: Loop the two bars around the hard change in the song's own rhythm, 10 bpm under this week's tempo. Then add a bar either side. Then the whole section.

drills.title: Random pairs
drills.instructions: Write the 16 chord names from the chord page on scraps of paper. Draw two, do one-minute changes, write the pair and the count on the back of the sheet. Draw again.

drills.title: Triad grip slide
drills.instructions: The Reckoner riff is one grip: middle finger on string 3, one fret above an index mini-barre on strings 2–1. C/E = 9-8-8, D = 11-10-10. Slide C → D → C, one shape per click at 60, the index never leaving the strings. Then add Em/G: index flat across strings 3-2-1 at fret 12. Teacher's riff shapes instead? Slide those.

drills.title: One-finger variations
drills.instructions: One bar each, four down-strums, metronome 70 → 90; only the named finger moves. **A** x02220 → Asus4 x02230 (add little finger) → A → Asus2 x02200 (lift ring) → A. **D** xx0232 → Dsus4 xx0233 → D → Dsus2 xx0230 → D. **C** x32010 → Cmaj7 x32000 (lift index) → C → C7 x32310 → C. **Rock G** 320033 → Cadd9 x32033 → Dsus4 xx0233 → Em7 022033.

drills.title: Scale in 3rds
drills.instructions: In this week's scale play pairs a 3rd apart: C–E, D–F, E–G, F–A, G–B, A–C, B–D, C–E … to the top, then back down (in G: G–B, A–C, B–D …). Quarters at 60 until clean, then eighths.

drills.title: Scale, then its chords
drills.instructions: Play the scale up and down once. Then strum the key's chords, one bar each, saying the numbers aloud. **C:** C Dm Em F G Am = I ii iii IV V vi. **G:** G Am Bm C D Em (Bm = A-shape barre, fret 2). **Sevenths of C:** Cmaj7 x32000, Dm7 xx0211, Em7 022030, Fmaj7 xx3210, G7 320001, Am7 x02010. Then I–V–vi–IV: C G Am F and G D Em C.

drills.title: Sing and find the root
drills.instructions: Strum a chord. Hum its root (the note it is named after). Find that note on string 6 and on string 5 below fret 12, play it against the chord, say its name. Write the frets on the session page.

drills.title: Count 3+3+3+2
drills.instructions: Here Comes the Sun bridge. Metronome at 150 and call each click an eighth note. Say “1-2-3 1-2-3 1-2-3 1-2”, one strum on each “1”: F, C, G, D. Then one 4/4 bar of D and a 7/8 bar of A7 counted “1-2 1-2 1-2-3”. Five clean passes, then +10.

drills.title: Make something
drills.instructions: Pick a home chord (Em or G). Choose three more shapes from the chord page. Loop them four beats each. Every pass change one thing: the order, one colour (sus2/sus4/maj7/add9), or the rhythm. Keep the version you'd want to play again; write it in the session's Notes line.

benchmarks.name: 5 · G major open position, eighths, top clean bpm

checkin: Reckoner: which sections do you play with the record? Which voicings did your teacher change?
Did the triad grip get easier from week to week? (yes / slowly / no)

sessions.name: A
sessions.title: Chord day
sessions.focus: New shapes and this week's three pairs (week plan, column 1). Pair 1 is the hard one.

blocks.title: Primer: today's shapes
blocks.instructions: Triad grip slide at 60 (2 min). Then air shapes ×10 and place-and-lift ×20 on the two chords of pair 1.

blocks.title: Pair 1: the full recipe
blocks.instructions: Anchor hunt (say what stays, slides, jumps) → slow motion ×5 → change loop to 10 clean → tempo ladder from 50, one chord per bar. Stop at the clock even if it's going well.

blocks.title: Pairs 2 and 3
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean on each, then one-minute changes: two rounds each. Write the better count.

blocks.title: One-finger colours
blocks.instructions: The A, D, C and rock-G lines from the drill page, one bar each. Last pass with eyes closed.

blocks.title: Fretboard: this week's key
blocks.instructions: This week's scale once up and down in quarters at 60, then its chords one bar each, saying the numbers.

blocks.title: Song: put pair 1 back in Reckoner
blocks.instructions: Song loop on the two bars with pair 1, then this week's section ×3 at this week's tempo.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick A, write the minutes. In Notes: the change that felt worst today.

sessions.name: B
sessions.title: Fretboard day
sessions.focus: Keys, scales and numbers, then chords applied in a key. Scale and key: week plan, column 2.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1, then the same change with eyes closed ×10.

blocks.title: This week's scale
blocks.instructions: Say the root name every time you play a square. Quarters at 60 until clean, then eighths on the tempo ladder. Weeks 2 and 4: in 3rds.

blocks.title: Scale, then its chords
blocks.instructions: Scale once, then the key's chords one bar each, saying the numbers (week 2: the sevenths). Then I–V–vi–IV in this week's key and in the other one.

blocks.title: Sing and find the root
instructions: Reckoner's chords Em, D, C, A: strum each, hum the root, find it on string 6 and string 5. Write the frets (string 6 / string 5):

blocks.title: Song by numbers: Here Comes the Sun
blocks.instructions: Capo 7. Verse D D G A7 = I I IV V. Verse ×4 with leave-early on every change, then the refrain at this week's tempo. Change-loop refrain bar 6 (Em7/G – D/F♯ – Em) first. Count the 7/8 bar: 1-2 1-2 1-2-3.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick B, write the minutes. Notes: anything in the scale you still have to look at.

sessions.name: C
sessions.title: Song day
sessions.focus: Longest song block: isolate this week's hard change (pair 1), then play the section and the song in time.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Place-and-lift ×20 and air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1.

blocks.title: The hard change
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean, then tempo ladder one chord per bar from 50. Thumb chord in the pair? Bass first.

blocks.title: Fretboard: E minor
blocks.instructions: G major open position from low E to high E (= E natural minor), quarters at 60. Then say Reckoner's verse in numbers: Em i, D ♭VII, C ♭VI, A IV.

blocks.title: Reckoner
blocks.instructions: Song loop round the hard change (5 min). This week's section ×3 at this week's tempo. Then the whole form at the same tempo without stopping — fumble through. Weeks 3–4: the last 5 minutes with the record.

blocks.title: Here Comes the Sun
blocks.instructions: Bridge: count 3+3+3+2 out loud, one strum per group — F C G D (3 min). Then the whole song at this week's tempo, leaving early on every change.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick C, write the minutes. Notes: the bar where you stopped, if any.

sessions.name: D
sessions.title: Mix and measure
sessions.focus: Short versions of everything, the benchmarks with numbers, and five minutes of your own music.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×5 on each chord in benchmarks 1–4 (log page). Nothing more — the tests are taken cold.

blocks.title: Benchmarks
blocks.instructions: One-minute changes, one round each, cold: **1** Em/G (12-12-12) ↔ D (11-10-10) · **2** C/E (9-8-8) ↔ Em/G · **3** Emaj7/G♯ ↔ Em/G · **4** Em7/G ↔ D/F♯. Then G major open position in eighths: tempo ladder from 60. Write all five numbers in this week's column of the log.

blocks.title: Keys from memory
blocks.instructions: On the back of this sheet write the six chords of C and of G with their numbers. Check against the drill page. Then play G's six, eyes closed.

blocks.title: Songs, measured
blocks.instructions: Reckoner, whole song (with the record from week 3; before that at this week's tempo). Then Here Comes the Sun. Write benchmarks 6 and 7 in the log.

blocks.title: Make something
blocks.instructions: Home chord Em or G plus three shapes from the chord page, four beats each, looped. Each pass change one thing: order, one colour, or the rhythm. Write the keeper (chords and strum) in Notes.

blocks.title: Log and exit check
blocks.instructions: Tick D in the log. Tick any exit box you passed today. Week 6 or all boxes ticked? Fill in the check-in sheet.
